'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****Russia reports a record for the ninth consecutive day of 113,122 new [[COVID-19]] cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.61 million. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2022/01/29/russia-sees-over-100000-daily-covid-19-cases-for-first-time-a76196 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 94,783 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkey-logs-record-94783-covid-19-cases-2022-01-29/ (''Reuters'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
***[[South Korea]] reports a record for the fourth consecutive day of 17,542 new COVID-19 cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 811,122. [http://m.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20220129000037 (''The Korea Herald'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2022 Russian military exercise controversy]]
**[[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Ireland)|Irish Minister for Foreign Affairs]] [[Simon Coveney]] announces that the [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Russian Minister of Defence]] has agreed to his request that the exercises would be moved outside the Irish [[Exclusive Economic Zone]]. '''Law and crime'''
*[[Freedom Convoy 2022]]
**Participants in the convoy arrive at [[Parliament Hill]] in [[Ottawa]], [[Ontario]], [[Canada]] to protest vaccine mandates and other public health restrictions imposed during the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://ottawa.ctvnews.ca/downtown-ottawa-roads-businesses-shut-down-as-freedom-convoy-protesters-flood-parliament-hill-1.5759563 (CTV News Ottawa)] 

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 Italian presidential election]]
**After seven inconclusive ballots, [[Sergio Mattarella]] is elected for a second term as [[President of Italy|President]] on the eighth ballot. [https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/politica/2022/01/29/quirinale-settima-votazione_f4e2081f-a15b-4c7c-b2e5-16632534c48f.html (ANSA)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022 Australian Open]]
**[[Tennis in Australia|Australian tennis]] player [[Ashleigh Barty]] defeats [[Tennis in the United States|American]] [[Danielle Collins]] in two [[Tennis scoring system#Set score|sets]], 6–3, 7–6,<sup>(7–2)</sup> to win the [[2022 Australian Open – Women's Singles|women's singles]] title at the [[Australian Open]]. Barty is the first home player to win the title since [[Chris O'Neil (tennis)|Chris O'Neil]] in [[1978 Australian Open – Women's Singles|1978]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20220129-battling-barty-breaks-44-year-hoodoo-to-win-australian-open (AFP via France 24)]
